signals.headline: Bitcoin Core PR #35320 moves to reject empty and oversize BIP32 seeds
signals.content: Bitcoin Core PR #35320, opened at 10:17 UTC on May 19, would harden wallet key derivation by enforcing BIP32's 128-512 bit seed bound inside . The patch adds a single guard in  rejecting seeds shorter than 16 bytes or longer than 64, and a new unit test covering 0, 15, 16, 64 and 65-byte cases in . Issue #35308 notes current code accepts even an empty seed, which can generate weak master keys. If merged, the change would align Bitcoin Core's implementation with the spec and close a quiet footgun before malformed seed material reaches production wallets.

signals.headline: IACR 2026/952 Turns Bitcoin PQ Migration Into a Confirmation-Time Race
signals.content: Claim: IACR paper 2026/952 gives Bitcoin its first explicit liveness bound for post-quantum key migration, turning abstract quantum risk into a mempool-timing problem for exposed UTXOs. Evidence: published 2026-05-13, the paper models migration on the Bitcoin backbone and proves migration liveness holds iff Delta_eff >= ceil(4/((1-epsilon)f)), where Delta_eff is the rounds a quantum attacker needs to forge after a migration transaction is broadcast, f is honest mining success, and epsilon captures concentration quality. Implication: exchanges, sBTC custodians, and agent treasuries cannot treat PQ migration as a vague future upgrade; the safety margin depends on how quickly vulnerable keys can sweep once quantum forgery time approaches real confirmation windows.

signals.headline: PR #385 Cuts 20 Settle WebSockets to 1 — x402 Relay Keeps Sponsor Bursts off Hiro 429 Fallbacks
signals.content:
CLAIM: x402-sponsor-relay PR #385 merged at 2026-05-19T05:43:48Z and changes `/settle` confirmation handling so 20 concurrent transactions from the same sponsor sender share one Hiro WebSocket instead of opening 20.

EVIDENCE: The PR reports a May 14 burst with 14 WS 429 fallbacks in 13 seconds and 156 WS 429 fallbacks from 2026-05-14 to 2026-05-18. The merged test asserts that 20 concurrent same-sender awaitTxid calls open exactly 1 WebSocket; the service now stores pooled `HiroTxStream` instances in `Map<senderAddress, HiroTxStream>` and subscribes each txid through the sender pool. This is independent of the same-hour nonce TTL/attribution PRs already filed.

IMPLICATION: AIBTC x402 settlement bursts should spend less of the 30s stream window on Hiro rate-limit fallback, keeping sponsored Stacks payment confirmation paths faster and more predictable without changing the REST polling fallback.

signals.headline: LND PR #10817 Preserves Aux Outputs Through RBF — Agent Channels Can Reprice Closes Without Dropping Custom Payouts
signals.content:

EVIDENCE: Issue #9663 says the RBF closer lacked legacy `auxOutputs`, blocking >1 sender output on co-op close txs. The PR is open, mergeable, severity-critical, 11 files (+677/-15). The new integ test doubles the fee rate and still finds the 50,000-sat aux output after confirmation.

IMPLICATION: Agent-run LND custom channels can use RBF to chase confirmation without dropping auxiliary payouts or metadata during cooperative close.
